spec: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_REAL_TIME_WRIGHT_FLYER_SIM_WITH_FRANKENSIM.md (ROUND 6 steady state), E1.9 / plan Round-3+4 convention decisions
no_claims: this dossier freezes CONVENTIONS (definitions, symbols, denominators, boundaries); the NUMERICAL values quoted as examples remain [V]/[V?] pending E1.2 source verification and must not be pinned into goldens from here
code-side identity registration of this schema constant lands with its first consumer (fs-flyer, E3.1), per register-at-introduction law

aspect_ratio.rule: bare 'AR' is BANNED in UI, dossiers, validation receipts, and code identifiers; every use names its denominator

AR_plane.definition: b^2 / S_one_plane — span squared over ONE wing plane's area

AR_system.definition: b^2 / S_both_planes — span squared over the TOTAL biplane lifting area

span_symbols.b: FULL wingspan [m]; never the semispan (many aerodynamics texts use b for semispan — this project does not)
span_symbols.s: semispan = b/2 [m]; the only admitted semispan symbol

ground_effect_reference.h: height of the LOWER main-wing quarter-chord reference plane above the aerodynamic ground plane [m]
ground_effect_reference.h_over_b: the primary ground-effect similarity variable; UI additionally displays h/c and lower-surface clearance
ground_effect_reference.aerodynamic_ground_plane: the FlatnessCertificate's fitted plane, NOT raw terrain height under the CG

control_surface_areas.convention: PROJECTED planform area onto the surface's reference plane (not developed/fabric area, not including framing gaps)
control_surface_areas.canard: sum of BOTH elevator planes' projected areas; per-plane values always available alongside the sum
control_surface_areas.rudder: sum of both movable vertical-surface projected areas; the 20-vs-21 ft^2 source discrepancy is a VALUE question for E1.2 under this convention, not a convention question
control_surface_areas.reference_area_for_coefficients: S_both_planes (total biplane lifting area) for aircraft-level coefficients; per-surface coefficients use that surface's own projected area, always labeled

mass_boundaries.rule: no single ambiguous 'engine weight' may enter the mass build-up; every mass names its boundary
mass_boundaries.engine_dry_kg: block, pistons, crank, valvetrain, intake — no fluids, no accessories
mass_boundaries.engine_installed_kg: engine_dry + mounts + fuel plumbing at the engine
mass_boundaries.drivetrain_kg: chains, sprockets, guides, propeller shafts and their bearings
mass_boundaries.propulsion_total_kg: sum of the above six buckets; the ONLY admitted aggregate
mass_boundaries.note: the NPS 170 lb vs ~180 lb literature spread is expected to resolve as different boundary choices; E1.2 assigns sourced values per bucket

provenance.derivation: plan Round-3 finding #4 (AR conventions), Round-3 historical flags (rudder area, engine mass), Round-2 Q20 (h/b), integrated through the six-round review
provenance.consumers: fs-flyer derived-quantity panel (E3.1), FlatnessCertificate (E4.4a), V-06 ground-effect cases, evidence-UX displays (E8.3a), flyer-reference.json (E1.2)
